name: Variable-Ratio Reinforcement
description: Rewarding a behavior after an unpredictable number of responses, rather than a fixed number or fixed interval, produces high and steady response rates with minimal pausing after reward, and makes the behavior markedly more resistant to extinction than behavior reinforced on a continuous or fixed schedule.
design_relevance_note: The mechanism most directly cited behind habit-forming product design (pull-to-refresh feeds, loot boxes, unpredictable notification timing) -- carries real ethical weight, since the same mechanism that drives slot-machine play drives compulsive app-checking.
prevalence_note: The named mechanism behind essentially every 'habit-forming design' and gamification framework in modern product design writing.

findings.description: The classic partial-reinforcement extinction effect (behavior trained under intermittent reinforcement resists extinction more than behavior trained under continuous reinforcement) can be reconciled with behavioral momentum theory: after extended training, continuous reinforcement actually yields a shallower extinction slope than raw comparisons suggest, situating intermittent reinforcement's extinction resistance within a broader account of reinforcement history strengthening resistance to disruption.
findings.source_title: Behavioral momentum and the partial reinforcement effect

findings.description: Variable-ratio reinforcement schedules — where reward follows an unpredictable number of responses — produce high, steady response rates with minimal post-reinforcement pausing, and behavior maintained on variable-ratio schedules is markedly more resistant to extinction than behavior maintained under continuous or fixed-schedule (fixed-ratio/fixed-interval) reinforcement.
